title: High-touch contractual feature queue and split-delivery protocol
creator: Ava Chen
description: Define and operationalize a deterministic pathway for high-touch enterprise feature requests that are contractually sensitive. The protocol will let Product negotiate partial deliveries (split-delivery) across releases, maintain clear SLA commitments, and place items into a contract-grade queue with visibility and gating for Eng/Legal/Sales. This reduces ad-hoc scope creep, shortens negotiation cycles with top accounts, and preserves predictable roadmap commitments for the broader product portfolio.
background: Over the past 18 months we've seen an increase in enterprise escalations requesting tailored features with contractual delivery dates. Current handling is ad-hoc: PMs promise delivery windows, Eng teams scramble, Legal reviews late. This causes missed commitments, strained renewals, and roadmap churn. There is no standard for carving a deliverable into an initial MVP surface (API/console) and a follow-up completion phase, nor clear SLOs for response / negotiation. Sales and CS ask for deterministic runways to communicate to customers.
goals: Create a formal contractual queueing process for enterprise feature asks
Define split-delivery patterns so we can ship minimal contractual scope early and finish remaining scope later
Establish time-to-response and negotiation SLOs (Triage-72h, Proposal-2 weeks, Commit-window negotiation within 30 days)
Provide a scoring rubric so PM/Eng/Sales can prioritize fairly and defensibly
Reduce roadmap churn from contractual requests by 40% within two quarters
scope_included: Intake form and rubric for scoring; Playbook for split-delivery (MVP / Complete); contract language templates; Console visibility for queued items; Pilot with 4 strategic accounts; integration with release train and rollout policies.
scope_excluded: Major core architecture rewrites; platform-level SLAs for hosted vs private deployments (these will be covered by separate Dedicated/Private SLA workstreams).
proposal: 1) Intake: implement a mandatory enterprise intake form that captures ARR, renewal date, compliance constraints, integration complexity, and legal dependencies. 2) Scoring: introduce a composite score (Revenue * 0.6 + RenewalRisk * 0.2 + StrategicFit * 0.2) normalized to 0-100. 3) Queue: create a contract-grade queue in the Console (read-only for customers) showing status: Triage / Proposal / Negotiation / Committed / Delivered. 4) Split-delivery templates: define patterns (API-first, Console-minimal, Docs/SDKs later) with acceptance criteria per pattern. 5) Contract templates: provide Legal-approved clauses for phased delivery and acceptance gates. 6) Operational SLOs for PMs and Sales with clear escalation path to a cross-functional gate meeting for any item with score > 70.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form collects required fields and blocks incomplete submissions
Scoring computes and surfaces a numeric score deterministically
Console shows queue entries with status and expected delivery windows
Two split-delivery templates are documented and approved by Eng and Legal
Pilot completed with 4 accounts and at least one split-delivery executed
Playbook validated in a tabletop exercise with Sales, CS, PM, Eng, Legal
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (4 weeks): build intake form (PM + Solutions Eng), scoring rubric, and one-pager. Phase 2 (6 weeks): Console queue prototype, contract templates with Legal, two split-delivery templates. Phase 3 (8 weeks): pilot with four accounts, monitor metrics, capture feedback. Phase 4 (Ongoing): iterate and add automation for queue updates and telemetries into the roadmap dashboard.
measurement: Time from intake to proposal (target <= 14 days)
Percent of enterprise requests using split-delivery after pilot (target >= 60%)
Contractual misses (failed committed dates) reduction (target -40% vs baseline)
CS / Sales NPS for negotiation experience (target +10 points)
Number of roadmap scope reversions caused by enterprise asks (target -30%)
dependencies: LEGAL-334 (Contract templates and phased delivery language)
risks: Engineering capacity overload if multiple high-score items align to same release window
Legal negotiation delays if phased delivery clauses are not accepted by customers
Sales pressure to prioritize revenue over technical feasibility leading to tech debt
Customers may reject split-delivery if acceptance criteria aren't clearly measurable
mitigations: Introduce a commit budget per cycle and explicit gating at cross-functional review
Pre-clear phased-delivery clauses with top legal contacts and include fallback escrow language
Require a technical feasibility sign-off during the Proposal phase
Make acceptance criteria explicit and measurable; include acceptance tests where feasible
notes: Previous incidents: missed-commit-2025-09 (postmortem) highlighted lack of negotiation SLOs
